proposedFixtureCrosswalk.equivalent: Ax=b with A rows (1,1,1), (2,-1,1), (1,2,-1) and b column (6,3,2)
proposedFixtureCrosswalk.boundaryVerifier: The first coefficient row has all 1s; replacing absent entries or dropping a column changes the system.
det([[2,1],[1,1]])=1, so the inverse is defined and A^-1 b must reproduce x=[2,1].
det(A)=7; verify both A*A^-1=I3 and A*x=b using exact rational entries.
All 3 original equations must hold: 6, 3 and 2; rejecting a two-entry solution is mandatory.
The augmented zero row is [0,0|0], leaving a free parameter; do not accept a single example as the full set.
Subtracting twice the first equation yields [0,0|1], a contradiction.
det(A)=1*4-2*2=0, so the inverse is undefined regardless of entries supplied.
2x2 inverse times a 3-entry column is undefined, even if a student pads a solution with zero.
Coefficient row order x,y,z and the negative y sign must both be preserved.
A 2x3 matrix has no two-sided square inverse even if its rows are independent.
